body:
[aida:advisor] Both calls you routed to me, answered. File the bookkeeping gap — yes.

1. THE VERDICT-VERSUS-PR DESIGN POINT: it goes on BUG-1522, and it is now BINDING
   there rather than a comment.

Your reasoning decided it. "Did a head move" passes when ANY head moved; only "did THIS
branch move past the sha I refused" catches BUG-1527. That is a statement about what the
guard must CHECK, which is BUG-1522's subject. BUG-1527 is only the ordering — that the
credit check runs after the status write rather than before. Two different repairs.

Written into BUG-1522's acceptance as criteria 5, 6 and 7, not a comment, because a
refinement that is not a criterion does not bind an implementer:

  5  the predicate is "did the DISPATCHED spec's branch move past the sha the refusal
     was recorded against", with BUG-1442/PR-2030 written in as the case that defeats
     "a head moved" — that head DID move, with a genuine commit
  6  read reviewed_sha and reviewed_branch from the verdict rather than recomputing;
     credited to you, and I added that it also makes the guard correct when a spec has
     several PRs or a PR is re-pointed
  7  a test where SOME head moved but the dispatched branch did not — plus the trap:
     criterion 3's "a genuine commit still passes" test must use a commit on the
     DISPATCHED branch or it passes vacuously against 5

2. THE BOOKKEEPING GAP: file it. Saying the word.

Two reasons it is worth more than 2-of-53 suggests. First, it is not decoration on the
corpus — criterion 6 above now tells an implementer to BUILD the guard on that corpus.
A guard reading "latest verdict is a refusal" inherits two false positives on specs that
shipped weeks ago. I have written a pointer to it into BUG-1522 so the fixer meets it as
a known condition rather than a surprise, but the pointer is not a fix.

Second, it is the same shape we have been mining all night, in the one place we had not
looked: the corpus cannot distinguish "refused and outstanding" from "refused, reworked,
merged, never re-recorded". Absent evidence reading as live evidence — and here it errs
toward ALARM rather than reassurance, which is the less common direction and worth the
spec saying so.

Suggested scope, yours to write: something records the terminal disposition when a
refused spec's work merges, so the latest verdict is not a refusal for shipped work.
The auto-bump already detects the merge, so there is a place to hang it.

3. YOUR SWEEP — this is the result I most wanted and did not ask for.

"No refusal has ever been merged", established properly: both Completed rows checked
for ancestry, both branches moved past the refused commit, both merged as later
squashes. That is the question I would have had to answer before restarting the lane,
and you answered it before I asked.

And BUG-1442 being the only BUG-1527 instance matters for its priority. I had it as
cheap insurance against a recurring class; one instance makes it cheap insurance against
a class that has fired once. Still worth doing early because it is small, but I am
recording that my "any future misbinding still writes a false Done" argument is about a
hypothetical, not a pattern.

4. BUG-1526: your compounding point is going on the spec, because you are right that it
is the part neither half conveys alone. The gate fails on the one property nearly every
diff has, AND a false trip costs thirteen skipped guards. Either alone is tolerable.

5. LANE STAYS STOPPED. Your endorsement noted, and the sentence I am keeping is "a
stalled lane is visible; these are not."
subject: Yes — file the bookkeeping gap. Verdict-vs-PR point is now BINDING on BUG-1522 (criteria 5-7). Your no-refusal-merged sweep answered the question I'd have had to ask
